result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and traffic signals but lacks dedicated pedestrian signal heads. The one-way street design and wide lanes suggest a vehicle-oriented environment with minimal physical protection for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: Pedestrians must rely on vehicular signals which may not provide adequate clearance time or a dedicated phase.

hazards.name: Wide one-way street
hazards.description: The wide, multi-lane one-way configuration encourages higher vehicle speeds and increases pedestrian exposure.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to improve predictability and safety for crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program the signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of formal crossing infrastructure and narrow, obstructed sidewalks. The absence of lane markings and the presence of parked vehicles on both sides of the street create potential visibility and safety issues for people walking.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to indicate where pedestrians should cross the street, increasing the risk of conflict with vehicles.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Cars parked along both sides of the street can block the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the foreground roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: A utility box and a person sitting on the narrow sidewalk on the right restrict the clear path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Add center lines and parking lane markings to organize traffic flow and reduce vehicle speeds.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked zebra crosswalk and a sidewalk, but is dominated by a wide roadway passing under a highway bridge. The lack of visible pedestrian signals and the deep shadows created by the overpass reduce the overall safety and comfort for people walking.

hazards.name: Shadowed Underpass
hazards.description: The highway overpass creates deep shadows that can obscure pedestrians from the view of oncoming drivers.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signals are visible to manage the crossing at this wide intersection.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear right-of-way and timing information.

interventions.title: Under-bridge Lighting
interventions.description: Improve lighting under the overpass to increase visibility of pedestrians and the roadway.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised refuge island in the center of the roadway to reduce crossing distance and exposure.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility crosswalks and pedestrian signals, but the wide roadway and lack of physical buffers like refuge islands increase pedestrian exposure. A large grassy embankment on one corner may also create sightline issues for approaching traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide intersection requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes without a refuge island, increasing exposure time.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: The grassy embankment on the left may limit sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, grassy area

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a median refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide street in two stages.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.
